claims.statement: Meta documents an Instagram App Secret, shown in the App Dashboard Instagram business login settings, that is sent as client_secret in the Instagram API with Instagram Login token exchange.

sources.supports: Your Instagram App Secret displayed in App Dashboard > Instagram > API setup with Instagram login > 3. Set up Instagram business login > Business login settings > Instagram app secret.
sources.locator: Business Login for Instagram, client_secret parameter

claims.statement: Meta documents that the Instagram App ID and the Instagram App Secret are both shown under App Dashboard, Instagram, API setup with Instagram login, Set up Instagram business login, Business login settings, and are needed for the business login flow.

sources.supports: In the App Dashboard > Instagram > API setup with Instagram login > 3. Set up Instagram business login > Business login settings, you will need: Your app's Instagram App ID; Your app's Instagram App Secret
sources.locator: IDs from the Meta App Dashboard

claims.statement: Meta states that apps using Facebook Login for Business use the Meta app ID shown at the top of the Meta App Dashboard, while apps using Business Login for Instagram use the Instagram app ID shown in the Instagram API setup section, so the two app IDs are documented as different identifiers by login type.

sources.supports: Apps that use Facebook Login for Business will use the Meta app ID displayed at the top of the Meta App Dashboard for your app. Apps that use Business Login for Instagram will use the Instagram app ID displayed on the Instagram > API setup with Instagram login section of the dashboard.

claims.statement: Meta documents the Instagram App Secret as the client_secret form field of a POST to https://api.instagram.com/oauth/access_token that exchanges an authorization code (together with client_id, grant_type authorization_code, redirect_uri and code).

sources.supports: To get the access token, send a POST request to the https://api.instagram.com/oauth/access_token endpoint with the following parameters: ... client_secret set to your app's Instagram App Secret from the App Dashboard
sources.locator: Step 2. Exchange the Code For a Token

claims.statement: Meta documents the Instagram app secret as the client_secret query parameter of a GET to graph.instagram.com/access_token with grant_type ig_exchange_token, which exchanges a short-lived Instagram user access token for a long-lived one, and requires that this request be made in server-side code because it includes the app secret.

sources.supports: Requests for long-lived tokens must be made in server-side code. These requesting include your app secret which you never want to expose in client-side code or in an app binary that could be decompiled. ... grant_type set to ig_exchange_token ... client_secret set to your Instagram app secret
sources.locator: Step 3. Get a long-lived access token

claims.statement: The business login page's sample requests show client_secret as a short placeholder string and the page states no length, alphabet or prefix for the Instagram App Secret.

sources.supports: client_secret set to your app's Instagram App Secret from the App Dashboard

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.

openQuestions.question: Only existence is established; format is not stated in the page and has not been researched.

The pages read show a separate Instagram App ID and Instagram App Secret location in the App Dashboard but do not say in prose whether it is a different secret from the Meta app secret (meta:app-secret). The two stay separate candidates until a page settles it.

Meta documents separate dashboard locations and separate app IDs by login type (see the claims) but no page read says whether the Instagram App Secret is a different value from the Meta app secret (meta:app-secret) or the same secret shown in two places. The 32-character tool-corroborated length on the Meta app secret contract is tied to a facebook context word and is not extended to this role. A Meta statement would settle it.

No Meta page read states a prefix, alphabet or length for the Instagram App Secret; the evidence supports a role (issuance location, two documented carriers, server-side only) and no independent grammar.

Whether an appsecret_proof-style derived output (documented for the Meta app secret) applies to Instagram Login calls is not established by the pages read; no derived output is recorded for this role.
The Instagram App ID is documented as a required request parameter and appears in the authorization window flow; no page read calls it non-secret. Recorded as an unresolved benign sibling.
